findings.title: Cooperative publishers have no atomic namespace reservation
findings.trigger: Two normal publish calls for the same output/request, each with9MiB payload, are interleaved: B pauses after prediction before mkdir; A stages and passes its final check; B stages and fails capacity; A then commits successfully.

observed.Berror: summary allocated namespace/staging peak exceeds16MiB cap

findings.impact: Successful publication can leave18,935,808B in a namespace whose declared cap is16,777,216B. Counting retained failed stages is necessary but insufficient without mutual reservation across prediction, staging and commit.
findings.expected_behavior: A cooperative duplicate publisher must fail before consuming unreserved staging space, or wait under a transaction-wide reservation. Prediction through stage write, retained failure evidence, reentry and atomic publication must share the same exclusion/reservation. Merely adding another non-atomic allocation check does not close the race.
